Exercises agent resource node discovery and wiring for coded (vs low-code) agents.

7	Inspect the working directory and its ancestors. Compute the variables below — every later step branches on them. Re-running the flow is safe: each step is gated on these signals and skips itself when its work is already done.

22	**State signals are recomputed implicitly by reading the filesystem at the step that consumes them.** Steps that mutate state (Setup creates `.venv`; Build/Run can rerun `init` and update `entry-points.json`; Evaluate creates `evaluations/`; Delivery may write `UIPATH_PROJECT_ID` to `.env`) update the underlying files; later steps read fresh values, not the initial table. Treat the table above as a snapshot at flow start, not a frozen contract.
23	
24	## CLI Conventions
25	
26	| Command family | Accepts `--output json` |
27	|---|---|
28	| `uip login`, `uip login status`, `uip login tenant list`, `uip login tenant set`, `uip logout` | yes |
29	| `uip codedagent setup` | yes |
30	| `uip codedagent new`, `init`, `run`, `dev`, `eval`, `deploy`, `push`, `pull`, `invoke` | no (forwarded to the Python CLI) |
31	
32	Use `uip codedagent <cmd>`, not `uv run uipath <cmd>`. The wrapper injects session credentials (`UIPATH_URL`, `UIPATH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, org/tenant identifiers) from your `uip login` session into the Python subprocess; `uv run uipath` skips that injection.
33	
34	## Critical Rules
35	
36	- **NEVER add a `[build-system]` section to `pyproject.toml`**. No `hatchling`, no `setuptools`, no build backend. UiPath agents do not use a build system. Only include `[project]`, `[dependency-groups]`, and `[tool.*]` sections.
37	- **Always create a smoke evaluation set.** Every agent must include `evaluations/eval-sets/smoke-test.json` with 2-3 test cases covering the primary happy path (not exhaustive error-case coverage — the smoke set exists to catch regressions, not to fully validate behavior). Create it in the Evaluate step, not during Build.
38	- **Select a framework before writing any code.** If the prompt clearly implies a framework (e.g., mentions tools, RAG, multi-step orchestration, or a specific SDK), pick the best match. If the prompt is ambiguous, ask the user to choose from: Coded Function, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or OpenAI Agents.
39	- **Correct SDK import: `from uipath.platform import UiPath`** — not `from uipath import UiPath` (that path does not exist and will cause `ImportError`). Always instantiate `UiPath()` inside functions/nodes, never at module level.
40	- **Refresh the CLI's Python executable path after venv changes.** If `uip codedagent` reports that the UiPath CLI/Python executable is not recognized, or any error indicates a stale `uipathExePath`, activate the project venv and run `uip codedagent setup --force`. This rewrites the CLI configuration to point at the current `.venv` executable.
41	- **Auth check is one-shot.** Run `uip login status --output json` once, at step 5. If the user supplied environment + organization + tenant or explicitly asked to connect to a specific tenant, run the matching one-shot `uip login --organization "<ORG>" --tenant "<TENANT>" --output json` after the status check, even if another session is already logged in. Otherwise, the wrapper auto-refreshes tokens on subsequent cloud calls (no `uip login refresh` exists); re-auth only on a real `401`.
42	- **Use `uip codedagent run` from non-interactive shells.** `uip codedagent dev` auto-appends `--interactive`.
43	- **Runtime captures only the last node's delta as output.** `Annotated[list, operator.add]` reducers accumulate inside the graph but vanish from `--output-file` JSON and eval trajectories. 76	## `uipath.json`
77	
78	```json
79	{
80	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
81	  "runtimeOptions": {
82	    "isConversational": false
83	  },
84	  "packOptions": {
85	    "fileExtensionsIncluded": [],
86	    "filesIncluded": [],
87	    "filesExcluded": [],
88	    "directoriesExcluded": [],
89	    "includeUvLock": true
90	  },
91	  "functions": {}
92	}

95	**Key fields:**
96	- **`runtimeOptions.isConversational`** - scaffold defaults to `false` (single-shot). Building a chat/conversational agent? Flip to `true` BEFORE `uip codedagent init` so `entry-points.json` gets the chat shape. See [conversational-agents](../capabilities/conversational-agents.md).

100	### `packOptions.directoriesExcluded` for solution context
101	
102	When the agent project is registered in a solution and uploaded via `uip solution upload`, the agent directory is bundled into the solution archive. Set `directoriesExcluded` to keep Python build artifacts out of the archive:
103	
104	```json
105	"packOptions": {
106	  "directoriesExcluded": [".venv", "__pycache__"],
107	  "includeUvLock": true
108	}
109	```
110	
111	`.venv/` is hundreds of MB of installed wheels and breaks uploads. `__pycache__/` is ephemeral bytecode. Both regenerate from `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` on the target side. Without these exclusions, `uip solution upload` produces an oversized archive that can be rejected by Studio Web.
112	
113	- `isConversational: true` for chat-style agents.
114	- `packOptions` controls `.nupkg` contents at deploy time.

15	│   └── solution_folder/

19	## Pattern 2: Published Coded Agent
20	
21	The coded agent is deployed to Orchestrator as a standalone tenant resource. Any solution can reference it.
22	
23	**When to use:** reused across flows, independent versioning, already deployed.
24	
25	```bash
26	uip codedagent deploy --my-workspace
27	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
28	```
29	
30	**Capture the package key from the deploy command's own output** — `uip codedagent deploy` prints JSON containing the package `Key` (an Orchestrator-assigned GUID). That GUID is the `resourceKey` used in the flow node's `type` (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>`) and `model.bindings.resourceKey`. Always run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` after deploy to refresh the local flow registry cache, but do NOT depend on `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` to return the deployed agent — that search only enumerates built-in node types (`uipath.agent.autonomous`, etc.); user-deployed coded agents do not appear there, so an empty result is the *expected* state and is NOT a sign the deploy failed.
31	
32	Fallback discovery paths if the deploy output is unavailable or unparseable, **tried in order** — stop at the first one that returns the package:
33	
34	1. `uip or packages list --search "<agent-name>" --output json` (tenant feed listing). Returns 404 on tenants where the caller lacks `Orchestrator.Packages.View` scope — if so, move to (2).
35	2. `uip or processes list --folder-path "<FolderName>" --output json` if the agent was deployed via `--folder` rather than `--my-workspace`.
36	
37	If all paths return empty / 404, the deploy command's stdout JSON is authoritative — re-run the deploy and capture its output rather than chasing post-hoc discovery endpoints.
38	
39	For the flow node JSON shape, see the uipath-maestro-flow skill agent-plugin reference (Published variant). `model.section` is `"Published"`.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Pattern 3: Tool Resource for Another Agent
44	
45	The coded agent is a tool that another agent (inline or published) can call. Requires deploying the coded agent to Orchestrator first.
46	
47	**Resource file** at `<AgentProject>/resources/<ResourceName>/resource.json`:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "$resourceType": "tool",
52	  "type": "agent",
53	  "name": "MyCodedAgent",
54	  "description": "What this agent does (shown to the parent LLM for tool selection)",
55	  "location": "external",
56	  "properties": {
57	    "processName": "<CODED_AGENT_PROCESS_NAME>",
58	    "folderPath": "<FOLDER_PATH>"
59	  },
60	  "inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": { "userInput": { "type": "string" } } },
61	  "outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content":   { "type": "string" } } },
62	  "id": "<UUID>",
63	  "referenceKey": ""
64	}
65	```
66	
67	Coded agents use `location: "external"`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Pattern Comparison
72	
73	| Aspect | In-Solution (1) | Published (2) | Tool (3) |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| Node type | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (local, from `project add`) | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (Orchestrator-assigned) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` |
76	| Lifecycle | `uip solution upload` (single pass) | `uip codedagent deploy` | `uip codedagent deploy` |
77	| Runtime lookup | Studio Web projects API | Orchestrator Releases API | Orchestrator (via parent agent) |
78	| `model.section` | `"In this solution"` | `"Published"` or absent | n/a |
79	| Cross-flow reuse | No | Yes | Yes |
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Debug
84	
85	| Error | Cause | Fix |
86	| --- | --- | --- |
87	| Node doesn't resolve in SW (Pattern 1) | `resourceKey` was hand-invented rather than read from the resource file | Run `uip maestro flow registry list --local` and use the returned `resourceKey` (it matches `resource.key` in `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) |
88	| Agent not found in registry (Pattern 2/3) | Not deployed or registry stale | `uip codedagent deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
89	| Tool resource never called | Tool description too vague | Sharpen the `description` in `resource.json` |

1	# LangGraph Integration Guide
2	
3	How to build LangGraph agents that work with the UiPath platform. This guide covers project structure, entrypoint detection, LLM models, and common pitfalls.
4	
5	## Scaffolding a New Project
6	
7	If there is **no existing agent code**, scaffold a LangGraph project with:
8	
9	```bash
10	mkdir my-agent && cd my-agent
11	uip codedagent new my-agent
12	```
13	
14	This generates `main.py` (with a StateGraph template), `langgraph.json`, and `pyproject.toml`. Then modify `main.py` to implement your actual agent logic.
15	
16	> **Prerequisite:** `uipath-langchain` must be installed for the LangGraph template to be used. If you get a base template instead, install `uipath-langchain` first.
17	
18	## Project Structure
19	
20	LangGraph agents use a **different structure** from coded function agents. There are two supported patterns:
21	
22	### Pattern A: `langgraph.json` (Recommended for LangGraph)
23	
24	```
25	my-agent/
26	├── main.py               # LangGraph definition — exports `graph` variable
27	├── langgraph.json        # Graph configuration — maps names to graph variables
28	├── pyproject.toml        # Dependencies (must include uipath-langchain)
29	├── .env                  # Environment variables
30	└── ...                   # Generated by uip codedagent init
31	```
32	
33	**`langgraph.json`** tells the runtime where to find your graph:
34	
35	```json
36	{
37	  "graphs": {
38	    "agent": "./main.py:graph"
39	  }
40	}
41	```
42	
43	- `"agent"` — the entrypoint name (used with `uip codedagent run agent`)
44	- `"./main.py:graph"` — path to the Python file and the variable name (`file:variable`)
45	- The file can be named `main.py` or `graph.py` — just ensure the path matches
46	
47	### Pattern B: `uipath.json` with `functions`
48	
49	For agents that use `main.py` instead of `graph.py`:
50	
51	```
52	my-agent/
53	├── main.py               # LangGraph definition — exports `graph` variable
54	├── uipath.json           # UiPath config with functions mapping
55	├── pyproject.toml        # Dependencies
56	└── ...
57	```
58	
59	**`uipath.json`** maps the graph entrypoint:
60	
61	```json
62	{
63	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
64	  "runtimeOptions": {
65	    "isConversational": false
66	  },
67	  "packOptions": {
68	    "includeUvLock": true
69	  },
70	  "functions": {
71	    "graph": "main.py:graph"
72	  }
73	}
74	```
75	
76	### Which Pattern to Use?
77	
78	| Pattern | When to Use |
79	|---------|-------------|
80	| `langgraph.json` | New LangGraph projects, multi-graph setups |
81	| `uipath.json` functions | Existing UiPath projects adding a LangGraph graph |
82	
83	Both patterns require the `graph` variable to be a compiled `StateGraph` or `CompiledStateGraph`.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Required Dependencies
88	
89	Every LangGraph agent needs these in `pyproject.toml`:
90	
91	```toml
92	[project]
93	name = "my-agent"
94	version = "0.0.1"
95	description = "My LangGraph agent"
96	requires-python = ">=3.11"
97	dependencies = [
98	    "uipath",
99	    "uipath-langchain",
100	]
101	
102	[dependency-groups]
103	dev = [
104	    "uipath-dev",
105	]
106	```
107	
108	**Key point:** `uipath-langchain` is required — it registers the LangGraph runtime factory that enables `uip codedagent run`, `uip codedagent init`, and deployment to detect and execute your graph.
109	
110	For agents that use LLM calls, add the appropriate model dependency:
111	
112	```toml
113	dependencies = [
114	    "uipath",
115	    "uipath-langchain",
116	    "langgraph>=1.0.4",          # If using StateGraph directly
117	    "langchain-community",        # If using community tools (DuckDuckGo, etc.)
118	]
119	```
120	
121	---
122	
123	## LLM Models
124	
125	Use UiPath's LLM libraries instead of raw `langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI`. These route through UiPath's LLM Gateway for centralized model management and billing.
126	
127	### UiPathAzureChatOpenAI (Passthrough)
128	
129	Drop-in replacement for LangChain's `ChatOpenAI` that routes through UiPath's passthrough endpoint (Azure OpenAI API format). No API keys needed — usage consumes Agent Units from your UiPath account.
130	
131	Instantiate LLM clients inside graph nodes or functions — module-level instantiation fails during `uip codedagent init`. See [../lifecycle/build.md](../lifecycle/build.md) § Additional Instructions for the full rule.
132	
133	```python
134	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
135	
136	# Inside a graph node:
137	llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(
138	    model="gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18",
139	    temperature=0.7,
140	    max_tokens=4000,
141	    timeout=30,
142	    max_retries=2
143	)
144	```
145	
146	**Model names:** Pass the model identifier as a string. Run `uip codedagent list-models` to list the models available in your tenant.
147	
148	**Features:**
149	- No API key needed — uses UiPath authentication
150	- Supports streaming, structured output, and tool calling
151	- Integrates seamlessly with LangChain agents and RAG
152	
153	### UiPathChat (Normalized)
154	
155	Versatile model class supporting multiple vendors through UiPath's normalized LLM Gateway API. Ideal for multi-vendor strategies.
156	
157	```python
158	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathChat
159	
160	llm = UiPathChat(
161	    model="gpt-4o-2024-11-20",
162	    temperature=0.5,
163	    max_tokens=2000
164	)
165	```
166	
167	**Supported Models Include:**
168	- **OpenAI**: `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `o3-mini-2025-01-31`
169	- **Anthropic**: `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0`
170	- **Google**: `gemini-2.0-flash-001`
171	- **AWS & Others**: Additional models based on your region and account
172	
173	**Features:**
174	- Supports multiple model providers
175	- Custom streaming headers for compatibility
176	- Flexible model switching for cost/quality optimization
177	- Regional availability may vary by data residency requirements
178	
179	### Configuration Parameters
180	
181	Both models support these configuration options:
182	
183	- `temperature` (0-1): Controls randomness vs. determinism (default: 0.7)
184	- `max_tokens`: Maximum response length (default varies by model)
185	- `timeout`: API request timeout in seconds
186	- `max_retries`: Number of retries on transient failures (default: 2)
187	- `top_p`: Nucleus sampling parameter for diversity
188	- `frequency_penalty`: Reduce token repetition
189	- `presence_penalty`: Encourage new topics
190	
191	### Structured Output
192	
193	Both models support `with_structured_output()` for Pydantic schema validation:
194	
195	```python
196	from pydantic import BaseModel
197	
198	class Analysis(BaseModel):
199	    sentiment: str
200	    confidence: float
201	
202	llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
203	structured_llm = llm.with_structured_output(Analysis)
204	raw_dict: dict = await structured_llm.ainvoke("Analyze: I love this product!")
205	result: Analysis = Analysis.model_validate(raw_dict)
206	```
207	
208	### Model Selection Guide
209	
210	| Use Case | Class |
211	|----------|-------|
212	| Cost-conscious, general tasks | `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` |
213	| Complex reasoning, state-of-the-art | `UiPathChat` or `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` |
214	| Multi-vendor flexibility (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) | `UiPathChat` |
215	| Specialized domains (e.g., code) | `UiPathChat` with a Claude model |
216	
217	Run `uip codedagent list-models` to see the model strings available in your tenant and pass the exact `model_name` to the class constructor.
218	
219	---
220	
221	## Graph Definition
222	
223	### Input/Output Schemas
224	
225	Define `GraphInput` and `GraphOutput` as Pydantic models. These become the agent's schema for `uip codedagent init` and deployment:
226	
227	```python
228	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
229	
230	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
231	    query: str = Field(description="The user's question")
232	    max_results: int = Field(default=5, description="Max results to return")
233	
234	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
235	    answer: str = Field(description="The answer")
236	    sources: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Sources used")
237	```
238	
239	### State Definition
240	
241	Use `MessagesState` for agents that need conversation history, or a plain `TypedDict`/`BaseModel` for simpler workflows:
242	
243	```python
244	from langgraph.graph import MessagesState
245	
246	class GraphState(MessagesState):
247	    query: str
248	    answer: str | None = None
249	    sources: list[str] | None = None
250	```
251	
252	### Building the Graph
253	
254	```python
255	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph
256	from langgraph.types import Command
257	
258	async def search(state: GraphState) -> Command:
259	    # ... your logic ...
260	    return Command(update={"answer": "result", "sources": ["url1"]})
261	
262	builder = StateGraph(GraphState, input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput)
263	builder.add_node("search", search)
264	builder.add_edge(START, "search")
265	builder.add_edge("search", END)
266	
267	graph = builder.compile()
268	```
269	
270	**Important:** The variable MUST be named `graph` and be a `CompiledStateGraph`. This is what the runtime factory looks for.
271	
272	### Runtime Output Quirk — No Channel Reducers For Output Fields
273	
274	The UiPath LangGraph runtime captures the **last node's update delta** as the final output (`runtime.py` uses `stream_mode=["updates",...]` and overwrites `final_chunk` per event). Channel reducers like `Annotated[list, operator.add]` accumulate inside the graph but **do not appear in `--output-file` JSON or eval trajectories** — only the terminal node's delta does.
275	
276	For any aggregate field that must appear in the output, carry it forward explicitly instead of relying on a reducer:
277	
278	```python
279	return {"items": [*state.get("items", []), new_item]}
280	```
281	
282	Or have the terminal node compute the full aggregate and emit it.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## Tracing
287	
288	LangGraph agents get **automatic tracing** — you do NOT need `@traced()` on graph nodes. The UiPath LangGraph runtime instruments all node executions, LLM calls, and tool invocations automatically.
289	
290	Use `@traced()` only on helper functions **outside** the graph that you want to monitor:
291	
292	```python
293	from uipath.tracing import traced
294	
295	@traced(name="postprocess", span_type="tool")
296	async def postprocess(text: str) -> str:
297	    """This gets its own trace span because it's not a graph node."""
298	    return text.strip().lower()
299	```
300	
301	---
302	
303	## Running `uip codedagent init`
304	
305	After creating your graph, generate project configuration:
306	
307	```bash
308	uv sync
309	uip codedagent init
310	```
311	
312	### How Entrypoint Detection Works
313	
314	1. `uip codedagent init` loads all registered middleware via Python entry points
315	2. The `uipath-langchain` package registers a LangGraph middleware
316	3. The middleware checks for `langgraph.json` — if found, it handles init
317	4. If no `langgraph.json`, the standard init checks `uipath.json` `"functions"` field
318	5. The runtime imports your Python file and validates the `graph` variable
319	6. Input/Output schemas are extracted from the graph's `input`/`output` type annotations
320	
321	### Troubleshooting `uip codedagent init`
322	
323	**"No function entrypoints found"**
324	- Ensure `langgraph.json` exists with the correct `"graphs"` mapping, OR
325	- Ensure `uipath.json` has a `"functions"` entry pointing to your graph
326	- The file path and variable name must match exactly (e.g., `"./main.py:graph"`)
327	
328	**Import errors during init / authentication failures**
329	- `uip codedagent init` imports your Python file to introspect the graph
330	- Module-level `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()` or `UiPathChat()` will try to authenticate on import and fail
331	- **Fix: Move LLM instantiation inside functions/nodes, never at module level:**
332	  ```python
333	  # BAD — fails during uip codedagent init:
334	  llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
335	
336	  # GOOD — lazy initialization inside a node:
337	  async def my_node(state):
338	      llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
339	      return await llm.ainvoke(state["messages"])
340	  ```
341	
342	**Schema not detected**
343	- Ensure your `StateGraph` specifies `input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput` 
344	- The Input/Output classes must be Pydantic `BaseModel` subclasses
345	
346	---
347	
348	## Running Your Agent
349	
350	```bash
351	# With langgraph.json
352	uip codedagent run agent '{"query": "What is Python?"}'
353	
354	# With uipath.json functions (using the function name)
355	uip codedagent run graph '{"query": "What is Python?"}'
356	```
357	
358	The entrypoint name comes from the key in `langgraph.json` `"graphs"` or `uipath.json` `"functions"`.
359	
360	---
361	
362	## Conversational Agents
363	
364	For the cross-framework contract (the `isConversational` flag, local-run options), see `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md`.
365	
366	### In-Process Input
367	
368	Type the graph state's `messages` field as a list of `AnyMessage` with the `add_messages` reducer:
369	
370	```python
371	from typing import Annotated
372	from langchain_core.messages import AnyMessage
373	from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
374	from pydantic import BaseModel
375	
376	class State(BaseModel):
377	    messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], add_messages] = []
378	```
379	
380	`langgraph.graph.MessagesState` is the equivalent shorthand.
381	
382	The wire envelope (see `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md` § Wire Envelope) lands as the `messages` field; the `uipath-langchain` runtime converts each `UiPathConversationMessage` dict into a LangChain `HumanMessage` before the graph runs.
383	
384	### Two Implementation Options
385	
386	Both are valid — pick based on the agent's needs:
387	
388	- **Prebuilt ReAct agent** — `from langchain.agents import create_agent`. The input contract above is already wired in; just export the compiled graph from your entry point.
389	- **Custom graph** — any `StateGraph` topology consuming the same `messages` field. The first node can be fully deterministic (e.g. validation or routing) before any LLM call.
390	
391	### Local Run
392	
393	See `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md` § Running Locally for the `--keep-state-file` flag (required on every turn) and § Wire Envelope for the `turn1.json` shape.
394	
395	---
396	
397	## Available Tools
398	
399	The `uipath-langchain` package provides UiPath-specific LangChain tools:
400	
401	| Tool | Import | Purpose |
402	|------|--------|---------|
403	| Process invocation | `uipath_langchain.agent.tools import create_process_tool` | Trigger UiPath processes |
404	| Escalation (HITL) | `uipath_langchain.agent.tools import create_escalation_tool` | Send to human reviewer |
405	| Context search | `uipath_langchain.retrievers import ContextGroundingRetriever` | Search Context Grounding indexes |
406	| MCP tools | `uipath_langchain.agent.tools import open_mcp_tools` | Connect to MCP servers |
407	
408	> **Context Grounding retrieval in LangGraph:** always use `ContextGroundingRetriever` from `uipath_langchain.retrievers` — not `sdk.context_grounding.search()` / `search_async()`. The LangChain retriever integrates natively with the graph pipeline and auto-generates the correct `index` binding. See [../capabilities/context-grounding.md](../capabilities/context-grounding.md) for usage examples.

1	# Agent Node — Implementation
2	
3	Agent nodes invoke UiPath AI agents via node type `uipath.core.agent.{key}`. Coded (Python) agents always use this plugin; low-code (`agent.json`) agents use it only when they are a standalone project (in-solution sibling or published). Inline low-code agents (embedded as a UUID subdirectory inside the flow project) use `uipath.agent.autonomous` — see the [inline-agent plugin](../inline-agent/impl.md).
4	
5	The agent lives in one of two places:
6	
7	- **In this solution** — sibling project inside the current solution. `{key}` is the local `resource.key` minted by `uip solution project add` (written to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`). The runtime resolves the node via the Studio Web projects API after `uip solution upload`. The manifest in `definitions[]` carries `model.section: "In this solution"`.
8	- **Published** — deployed to Orchestrator as a tenant resource. `{key}` is the Orchestrator-assigned resource key. Discoverable via `uip maestro flow registry search`. The manifest in `definitions[]` carries `model.section: "Published"`.
9	
10	The node-instance shape (in `nodes[]`) is identical across the two variants — only the manifest in `definitions[]` differs (`{key}` and `model.section`).
11	
12	## Discovery
13	
14	**Published (tenant registry):**
15	
16	```bash
17	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
18	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent" --output json
19	```
20	
21	Requires `uip login`. Only published agents from your tenant appear.
22	
23	**In-solution (local, no login required):**
24	
25	```bash
26	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
27	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
28	```
29	
30	Run from inside the flow project directory. Discovers sibling agent projects in the same `.uipx` solution.
31	
32	## Registry Validation
33	
34	```bash
35	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.{key}" --output json
36	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.{key}" --local --output json
37	```
38	
39	Requires `uip login`. Only published agents from the tenant appear in the registry.
40	
41	Confirm from `registry get`:
42	
43	- Input port: `input`
44	- Output port: `output`
45	- `outputDefinition.output.schema` — contains `content` (string)
46	- `outputDefinition.error.schema` — contains `code`, `message`, `detail`, `category`, `status`
47	- `model.serviceType` — `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`
48	- `model.bindings.resourceSubType` — `Agent`
49	- `model.bindings.resourceKey` — the `<FolderPath>.<AgentName>` string used to scope binding resolution
50	- `inputDefinition` — typically empty (agents accept free-form input via the flow's wiring)
51	
52	## Adding / Editing
53	
54	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure below for the node-specific `inputs`.
55	
56	## JSON Structure
57	
58	### Node instance (inside `nodes[]`) — published variant
59	
60	The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and binding/context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`.
61	
62	```json
63	{
64	  "id": "classifyIntent",
65	  "type": "uipath.core.agent.ffa33d88-8a85-4570-933c-9a69aa2dfbb5",
66	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
67	  "display": { "label": "Classify Intent" },
68	  "inputs": {},
69	  "outputs": {
70	    "output": {
71	      "type": "object",
72	      "description": "The return value of the agent",
73	      "source": "=result.response",
74	      "var": "output"
75	    },
76	    "error": {
77	      "type": "object",
78	      "description": "Error information if the agent fails",
79	      "source": "=result.Error",
80	      "var": "error"
81	    }
82	  }
83	}
84	```
85	
86	The `model` block (BPMN type, `serviceType`, `bindings`, `context` template) lives on the manifest entry in `definitions[]`, not on the instance. The manifest is auto-populated by `uip maestro flow registry pull` — never hand-author it.
87	
88	Three values to discover — never invent:
89	- **`type` suffix** — Orchestrator-assigned UUID for this agent. Per-ring and per-agent — never copy across environments. Read from `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` / `registry get` as `nodeType`.
90	- **`typeVersion`** — the manifest's `version` field. Read from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json` (`.version`).
91	- **`resourceKey`** — composite `<FolderPath>.<AgentName>` (e.g. `Shared.Apple Genius Agent`). Appears on each top-level `bindings[]` entry tied to this agent. Read from `registry get` (`model.bindings.resourceKey` on the manifest).
92	
93	Confirm all three from `registry get` before wiring.
94	
95	### Node instance (inside `nodes[]`) — in-solution variant
96	
97	```json
98	{
99	  "id": "codedAgent",
100	  "type": "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>",
101	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
102	  "display": { "label": "<Label>", "icon": "<AGENT_ICON>" },
103	  "inputs": {},
104	  "outputs": {
105	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "The return value of the agent", "source": "=result.response", "var": "output" },
106	    "error":  { "type": "object", "description": "Error information if the agent fails", "source": "=result.Error", "var": "error" }
107	  }
108	}
109	```
110	
111	`<AGENT_ICON>` depends on the agent's implementation type: `"coded-agent"` for Python-coded agents, `"autonomous-agent"` for low-code (`agent.json`) agents. Detect the type by inspecting the sibling agent project directory: if `agent.json` exists at its root, use `"autonomous-agent"`; otherwise use `"coded-agent"`. Do NOT copy `.display.icon` from `uip maestro flow registry get --local` — that manifest returns `"coded-agent"` for every in-solution agent regardless of implementation type, and the value must be corrected here.
112	
113	Same shape as the published variant — no `model` on the instance.
114	
115	**Never hand-author the `definitions[]` entry.** Run `uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json`, extract the `Data.Node` object, and paste it verbatim into `definitions[]`. Constructing it by hand risks missing required validator fields (`model.section`, `runtimeConstraints`, `supportsErrorHandling`, etc.).
116	
117	`<resourceKey>` is the local `resource.key` written by `uip solution project add` to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json` — read it from that file or from `uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json`. Read `<DEFINITION_VERSION>` from `uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json` (`.version`).
118	
119	### Top-level `bindings[]` entries (sibling of `nodes`/`edges`/`definitions`)
120	
121	**Rule.** Exactly one entry per `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)` pair. Multiple node instances referencing the same agent MUST reuse the same `bindings[].id` — never duplicate the entry.
122	
123	**Validate.** After writing the flow, group `bindings[]` by `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)`. Each group must have length 1. If any group has length > 1, deduplicate before saving.
124	
125	```json
126	"bindings": [
127	  {
128	    "id": "bClassifyIntentName",
129	    "name": "name",
130	    "type": "string",
131	    "resource": "process",
132	    "resourceKey": "<resourceKey>",
133	    "default": "<agent-name>",
134	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
135	    "resourceSubType": "Agent"
136	  },
137	  {
138	    "id": "bClassifyIntentFolderPath",
139	    "name": "folderPath",
140	    "type": "string",
141	    "resource": "process",
142	    "resourceKey": "<resourceKey>",
143	    "default": "<folder-path-or-empty>",
144	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
145	    "resourceSubType": "Agent"
146	  }
147	]
148	```
149	
150	> For the resolution mechanics and why these entries are required, see [file-format.md — Bindings](../../../../shared/file-format.md#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings).
151	
152	## Accessing Output
153	
154	The agent's response is available downstream:
155	
156	```javascript
157	// In a Script node after the agent
158	const response = $vars.classifyIntent.output.content;
159	return { classification: response };
160	```
161	
162	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content` — the agent's text response
163	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the agent fails
164	
165	## If the Agent Does Not Exist Yet
166	
167	Create the agent first, then wire it. Three paths:
168	
169	- **In-solution (sibling project, coded or low-code)** — scaffold via `uipath-agents`, register with `uip solution project add` to mint the local `resource.key`, then discover via `uip maestro flow registry list --local`. For the coded pipeline, see [coded/embedding-in-flows.md](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded/embedding-in-flows.md).
170	- **Published coded agent** — `uip codedagent deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`.
171	- **Published low-code agent** — `uip solution deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`.

173	## Using an Agent as a Tool Resource
174	
175	To use a published agent (coded or low-code) as a **tool for another agent** rather than a standalone flow node, add it as a `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` resource node wired to the parent agent's `tool` handle. This lives within the agent's canvas, not at the top level of the flow.
176	
177	For the resource file format and wiring details, see the `uipath-agents` skill:
178	- Coded agents: [coded/flow-integration.md § Pattern 3](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded/flow-integration.md#pattern-3-tool-resource-for-another-agent)
179	- Low-code agents: see the `uipath-agents` skill's low-code references.

181	## Debug
182	
183	| Error | Cause | Fix |
184	| --- | --- | --- |
185	| Node type not found in registry | Agent not published, or registry stale | If in same solution: run `registry list --local`. Otherwise: run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`. For coded agents, ensure `uip codedagent deploy` completed successfully |
186	| In-solution node doesn't resolve | `resourceKey` was hand-invented rather than read from the resource file, or `uip solution project add` was never run for the agent project | Run `uip maestro flow registry list --local` and use the returned `resourceKey` (same value as `resource.key` in `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`) |
187	| Agent execution failed | Underlying agent errored | Check `$vars.{nodeId}.error` for details. For coded agents, test locally first with `uip codedagent run` |
188	| Empty `output.content` | Agent returned no response | Verify the agent is configured correctly (published: in Orchestrator; in-solution: in Studio Web) |
189	| `inputDefinition` is empty | Expected — agents accept input via flow wiring, not typed fields | Wire upstream data to the agent via `$vars` expressions |

1	# Greenfield — Create a New Flow
2	
3	End-to-end journey for creating a Flow project from scratch. Author terminates at `validate` + `format`. To publish, run, or debug after this, see [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md).
4	
5	> **Brownfield edits use a different journey.** If the `.flow` file already exists, see [brownfield.md](brownfield.md) instead.
6	
7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10	
11	**Plan when:**
12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach
15	
16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)
19	- The user has already described the exact topology they want
20	
21	### Examples
22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."
24	→ Multiple services, branching logic, connector discovery needed. Plan first.
25	
26	**Don't plan:** "Create a flow that calls an API and sends the result to Slack."
27	→ Linear pipeline, user knows what they want. Build directly, ask questions inline if needed. **"Build directly" skips the plan doc, not the registry search** — you still `registry search` each named service and pick a node type via the Step 3 ladder.
28	
29	**Judgment call:** "Build me a flow that processes invoices."
30	→ Ambiguous requirements. Ask clarifying questions; plan if answers reveal complexity.
31	
32	## Three-turn execution map
33	
34	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
35	
36	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s) **+** optional `uip login status`. **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
39	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
40	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
41	
42	### Batching anti-patterns
43	
44	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
45	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
46	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
47	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
48	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
49	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.
50	
51	## Step 0 — Resolve the `uip` binary and detect command prefix **[T1]**
52	
53	See [shared/cli-conventions.md](../../shared/cli-conventions.md) for binary resolution, version detection, and the `uip maestro flow` vs `uip flow` command prefix rule. All commands below are written in the `uip maestro flow` form. <!-- uip-check-skip -->
54	
55	This probe is read-only — emit as a parallel `Bash` alongside the Step 2 scaffold chain. It does not need its own turn.
56	
57	## Step 1 — Check login status **[T1 — only if needed]**
58	
59	Greenfield steps 2–6 work without login (`flow init`, `validate`, `format`, registry OOTB nodes, `Edit` / `Write` edits). Login is required only when the registry needs tenant-specific connector/resource nodes, or before handing off to Operate.
60	
61	```bash
62	uip login status --output json
63	```
64	
65	If not logged in and you need tenant nodes:
66	
67	```bash
68	uip login                                          # interactive OAuth (opens browser)
69	uip login --authority https://alpha.uipath.com     # non-production environments
70	```
71	
72	When you do need it, emit `uip login status --output json` as a parallel `Bash` inside T1.

74	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
75	
76	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so the solution name matches the project name rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
77	
78	Check for existing solutions with `ls *.uipx */*.uipx 2>/dev/null` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask via `AskUserQuestion`, presenting a dropdown with one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** as the last option. The user wanting a new solution does not let you skip this; you only learn that by asking. If none are found, create a new one automatically. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md).
79	
80	- If the user specifies an existing `.uipx` file path or solution name, use that (skip to Step 2b)
81	- Otherwise, create a new solution (Step 2a)

83	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
84	
85	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
86	
87	```bash
88	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
89	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
90	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
91	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
92	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
93	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
94	```
95	
96	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
97	
98	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
99	
100	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.
101	
102	The sub-steps below describe what each command in the chain does and how to verify the result.
103	
104	### 2a. Create a new solution
105	
106	```bash
107	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
108	```
109	
110	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
111	
112	> **Naming convention:** Use the same name for both the solution and the project unless the user specifies otherwise. If the user only provides a project name, use it as the solution name too.

114	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
115	
116	```bash

233	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
234	
235	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
236	
237	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
238	
239	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
240	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
241	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
242	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
243	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
244	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
245	
246	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)).
247	
248	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
249	
250	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
251	
252	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
253	
254	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
255	|---|---|---|
256	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
257	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. Empty after `flow init` (`\n  "edges": []`); the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
258	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
259	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in `init`-scaffolded flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
260	
261	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
262	
263	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
264	
265	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
266	
267	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
268	
269	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
270	
271	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

289	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
290	
291	```bash
292	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
293	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
294	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
295	```
296	
297	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
298	
299	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
300	
301	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
302	
303	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). 21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
46	
47	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by `uip maestro flow init` and packaging. Do not add them manually.
48	
49	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. 75	    "output": {

77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}

90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.

135	### Node outputs
136	
137	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
138	
139	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
140	
141	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
142	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
143	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
144	
145	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
146	
147	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
148	
149	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
150	- `description` — human-readable description
151	- `source` — runtime binding expression (e.g., `"=result.response"` for the primary output, `"=result.Error"` for errors)
152	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
153	
154	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector, agent):
155	
156	```json
157	"outputs": {
158	  "output": {
159	    "type": "object",
160	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
161	    "source": "=result.response",
162	    "var": "output"
163	  },
164	  "error": {
165	    "type": "object",
166	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
167	    "source": "=result.Error",
168	    "var": "error"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port:
174	
175	```json
176	"outputs": {
177	  "output": {
178	    "type": "object",
179	    "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
180	    "source": "=result.response",
181	    "var": "output"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).

188	## Layout
189	
190	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
191	
192	```json
193	"layout": {
194	  "nodes": {
195	    "start": {
196	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
197	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
198	      "collapsed": false
199	    },
200	    "rollDice": {
201	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
202	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
203	      "collapsed": false
204	    },
205	    "end": {
206	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
207	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
208	      "collapsed": false
209	    }
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
215	
216	**What format does:**
217	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
218	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
219	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
220	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
221	
222	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).

300	## Implicit error port on action nodes
301	
302	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
303	
304	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
305	
306	### When the error port fires
307	
308	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
309	- Request timeouts
310	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
311	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
312	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
313	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
314	
315	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`.
316	
317	### Wiring the error port
318	
319	```bash
320	# Confirm the node supports error handling
321	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
322	
323	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
324	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
325	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
326	```
327	
328	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself:
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
333	  "inputs": {
334	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
335	  }
336	}
337	```
338	
339	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
340	
341	### Error port vs other branching
342	
343	| Mechanism | When to use |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
346	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
347	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
348	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

467	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
468	
469	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). **Do not edit this file directly** — it is auto-generated by `uip maestro flow init` and regenerated by `uip maestro flow debug` before upload. Manual edits will be overwritten.

471	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
472	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes

478	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
479	
480	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
481	
482	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
483	
484	```json
485	"bindings": [
486	  {
487	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
488	    "name": "name",
489	    "type": "string",
490	    "resource": "process",
491	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
492	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
493	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
494	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
495	  },
496	  {
497	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
498	    "name": "folderPath",
499	    "type": "string",
500	    "resource": "process",
501	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
502	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
503	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
504	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
505	  }
506	]
507	```
508	
509	**Rules:**
510	
511	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
512	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
513	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
514	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
515	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
516	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
517	
518	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one.
